hints: Substitute base units into v = F^p * mu^q and collect powers of kg, m, and s.
Compare the power of s on both sides to find p first.
solution: (a) [v] = m s^-1, [F] = kg m s^-2, [mu] = kg m^-1. (b) m s^-1 = kg^(p+q) m^(p-q) s^(-2p). Equating powers: s: -2p = -1 => p = 1/2. kg: p + q = 0 => q = -1/2.
teacher_walkthrough: (a) Base units: speed is m s^-1; tension force is kg m s^-2; linear density is kg m^-1.
(b) Express right side in base units: (kg m s^-2)^p * (kg m^-1)^q = kg^(p+q) * m^(p-q) * s^(-2p).
Equate powers with left side (kg^0 m^1 s^-1):
Check length (m): p - q = 1/2 - (-1/2) = 1. Matches m^1.
Result: p = 1/2, q = -1/2 (giving v = C * sqrt(F / mu)).
